blocks.text: WASHINGTON, United States — Government agencies and companies around the world shut down websites Wednesday after two critical flaws came to light involving PHP, a programming language that is the basis for a large share of the internet. PHP sits underneath popular web design platforms, so the weaknesses potentially affect a vast range of websites, from online stores and news outlets to government services. Wiz, one of the security firms that found the flaws, estimated that PHP runs about 70 percent of the world’s websites and said they rank “among the most severe vulnerabilities discovered in PHP, and arguably in software history.” […]...
